summary: The exact candidate corrects the Muse answer-channel grammar boundary and removes the reported quadratic reasoning-history copies. However, its new history-slice calculation makes rollback(0) roll back every inner-grammar generation token while leaving wrapper state unchanged. This candidate-only state inconsistency requires a narrow correction and regression test.

tests.what_was_measured: Imported the prepared source path and reproduced first grammar masking at position 6 versus answer-body position 11; the five Muse answer-header tokens were fed to the grammar.

First grammar masking moved to answer-body position 11; only body tokens were accepted. A 2,000 reasoning + five header + 2,000 answer stream had 4,006 snapshots, zero nested history lists/copies, and rollback restored the reasoning state.
155 tests and 64 subtests passed at the exact candidate commit.
Positive rollback depths matched clean replay across a repeated-channel deterministic case and 500 randomized cases, but rollback(0) emptied the inner grammar and was not a no-op.
Base preserved inner accepted tokens [20, 21] after rollback(0); candidate changed them to [] while tokens_after_end stayed 2.
All candidate-changed Python source compiled successfully.

gpu_execution.evidence: The reproduced boundary, storage, and rollback defects are deterministic Python state-machine behavior and require no GPU kernel or model execution.

remaining_counterexamples: At b52daa1dd1564889b9eb2e59ef8c6bfcd7e32091, ReasonerGrammarObject.rollback(0) evaluates self._state_history[-0:] as the entire history, rolls back every inner-grammar generation token, and leaves tokens_after_end unchanged.
remaining_limitations: Muse Glimmer 30B NVFP4 weights were unavailable; production placeholder frequency, semantic output quality, and the full HTTP serving path were not reproduced.
No native source changed, so native rebuild validation was not applicable.
No GPU execution was performed because the reviewed behavior is CPU-side Python state management.
